newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf Coast conspicuously bereft of Brent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf Coast conspicuously bereft of Brent.

text.p: No sooner had offers for Brent crude oil into the U.S. Gulf Coast appeared late last week than they receded yet again, leaving the Atlantic Basin awash in crude but bereft of the North Sea benchmark, traders said on Monday.
"There are no Brents, but there is lots of crude out there," a Gulf Coast buyer said.
Stasco, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell, had accumulated eight Brent cargoes last week, leaving the market in jitters over the consequent overhang.
The oil giant was heard to have given up on a transatlantic vayage. At the same time, the company sold one of its clutch to a Wall Street refiner on Monday at May Brent minus 94 cents a barrel.
Market sources speculated that Shell will retain most of the remaining barrels in its own refining system.
Other North Sea crudes remained plentiful. A Norwegian company was offering two Gullfaks cargoes for April 23-27 delivery, asking May West Texas Intermediate minus $1.00.
The Gullfaks cargoes had been coupled with two Troll cargoes that were already sold off a VLCC, traders said.
The same company sold the last of four Oseberg cargoes last Friday at May WTI minus $1.10 for April 25-30 delivery.
The U.S. buyer was heard to be reselling the cargo, asking May WTI minus 83 cents, although this could not be immediately confirmed.
From West Africa, Bonny Light and Qua Iboe were offered at dated Brent plus $1.75 a barrel delivered.
In Latin America, Cusiana was pegged around WTI minus $1.80-85 a barrel in a continuing weak trend tied to plentiful supplies.
Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol opened a tender for Cano Limon, loading May 7-12, trade sources said. The grade was last done around WTI minus $3.25 a barrel.
Venezuelan Mesa-30 showed continuing softness as well. The grade, which has a higher sulfur content than Cano Limon, was assessed at WTI minus $3.50-4.00 a barrel.
Elsewhere, Bolivia's state oil company YPFB was selling 260,000 barrels of reconstituted crude available for loading April 15, trade sources said.
Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) will receive bids on April 11.
Bolivia's reconstituted crude contains about 45 percent gasoline and has an API gravity of around 45 degrees.
The crude loads at the Chilean port of Arica.
